correctness.rationale: The exact cumulant generating functions give \(K_+(t)=t^2/2+\sqrt2 t^3/(3\sqrt m)+t^4/(2m)+O(t^5/m^{3/2})\) and \(K_0(t)=t^2/2+t^4/(2m)+2t^6/(3m^2)+O(t^8/m^3)\). At \(x\sim\sqrt{2\log p}\), the positive cubic term yields the shift \(4(\log p)^{3/2}/(3\sqrt m)\); the balanced saddlepoint rate \(I_m(x)=x^2/2-x^4/(2m)+4x^6/(3m^2)+\cdots\) yields shift \(2(\log p)^2/m\). The remainder ratios are \(o(1)\) under \(m/\log p\to\infty\). The gamma triangular-array theorem covers the positive row normalization, and the balanced tilting argument gives the stated tail ratio and shifted-Gumbel limits.
residual_risks: Anderson–Coles–Hüsler (1997) was available only through bibliographic/abstract material, so an older equivalent sign-sensitive paired formulation remains a low originality risk.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies spectral sign balance as a sharp phase coordinate invisible to the fourth-order effective rank: the Gaussianization requirement changes by a full logarithmic power and the critical error is quantified by an explicit Gumbel-translation profile. This is a natural boundary question in the motivating high-dimensional approximation problem.
residual_risks: The statement is restricted to independent flat spectra and does not classify partial sign imbalance.

limitations: Independent coordinates and flat equal-magnitude spectra only; exact balance is required for the log-squared threshold statement; the analysis assumes m/log p tends to infinity and excludes finite-sample U-statistic approximation error. Anderson–Coles–Hüsler (1997) was not inspected in full.
